primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis (hereditary xerocytosis) due to PIEZO1 gain-of-function
mechanism: Gain-of-function PIEZO1 variants slow inactivation or facilitate opening of the mechanically activated cation channel, increasing erythrocyte cation permeability and disrupting red-cell ion/volume homeostasis, which produces cellular dehydration and chronic hemolysis.
vignette: A 22-year-old woman has lifelong compensated hemolysis, mild jaundice, reticulocytosis, and iron overload despite never receiving transfusions. Her mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration is increased, and her erythrocytes have decreased osmotic fragility. Her father has similar findings. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PIEZO1.
lead: Which of the following changes in the mutant protein most directly explains this disorder?
correct: Slower inactivation of a mechanically activated cation channel, increasing erythrocyte cation permeability
distractors: Loss of spectrin self-association, causing membrane surface-area loss and spherocyte formation
Failure of the erythrocyte chloride-bicarbonate exchanger, preventing carbon dioxide transport
Gain-of-function of the erythrocyte Gardos potassium channel, increasing potassium efflux
Failure of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase to generate reduced glutathione
distractor_notes: Spectrin/ankyrin membrane-skeleton defects are typical mechanisms of hereditary spherocytosis, not PIEZO1-associated dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis.
Band 3/AE1 is the major erythrocyte chloride-bicarbonate exchanger; its dysfunction is not the PIEZO1 gain-of-function mechanism described here.

Gain-of-function KCNN4/Gardos-channel variants are a distinct cause of dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis; this patient instead has a pathogenic PIEZO1 variant whose defining defect is prolonged mechanosensitive cation-channel activity.
G6PD deficiency impairs protection from oxidant stress and causes episodic oxidative hemolysis, not an inherited mechanosensitive cation-channel disorder.
key_expl: PIEZO1 is a mechanically activated ion channel. Disease-associated gain-of-function variants commonly slow channel inactivation or make opening easier, increasing cation permeability and disturbing erythrocyte ion and volume homeostasis. The resulting dehydrated red cells undergo chronic hemolysis.
objective: Relate PIEZO1 gain-of-function and slowed mechanosensitive-channel inactivation to increased erythrocyte cation permeability and hereditary xerocytosis.
